name: A still frame breathes into a moving shot
looks: A close-up portrait of an animal holds completely still for a beat, read as a photograph, then its fur ruffles faintly and the camera starts a slow push in, revealing it was a video clip the whole time. A caption, "From stills to motion.", fades in low in the frame only after the motion has started.
build: Open on a single held frame (400-600ms) before playback starts, so the still-to-video cut is really just delayed playback. The giveaway motion (fur, a slow push-in) is subtle and physical, not an obvious effect. Caption fades in after motion is already visible, confirming rather than announcing.
sound: Near silence during the held frame, ambient sound fading up the instant motion starts.
prompt: Hold on a close shot that reads as a still photo a beat too long, then let it quietly start moving with subtle physical motion to reveal it was video all along, fading in a short caption only once the motion has already begun.
